title: Persist strict E2EE admission across OS services and harden WebRTC and release integrity.
changes: Add remcp e2ee status|require|off and preserve the owner requirement across Linux, macOS and Windows service restarts and updates. Hosted transport is still TLS-only; requiring E2EE refuses connection rather than silently downgrading.

Recheck local policy before live requests, reconnects and outgoing tool responses. Suppress an in-flight result or error and close the old connection if policy tightens or local configuration becomes unreadable.

Preserve the publicly released v0.2.257 Linux systemd parent-directory descriptor pinning, bounded unit reads, owner verification and symlink substitution rejection; no rollback to the v0.2.256 lifecycle.

Make the existing seven seeded, real fast-check browser destination and CDP security properties detectable as .test.js in the public source release; retain the same assertions, replay seeds and explicit runtime test invocation.

Add a pinned, least-privilege CodeQL JavaScript/TypeScript, Python, GitHub Actions and C# security workflow to the future public release. The existing Default Setup must remain enabled until the replacement workflow can genuinely upload analysis results after an explicitly controlled migration.

Require genuine GitHub OIDC/Sigstore SLSA provenance for the exact four tagged release assets, with byte-for-byte source matching, strict signer/ref/digest verification and release-local remcp-release.intoto.jsonl evidence. Refuse retroactive signatures and do not overwrite existing published assets during recovery.

Harden opt-in Windows WebRTC QA: hash the frozen worker executable through a pinned bounded descriptor (CodeQL #81), and pin private TURN credentials through the same owner/ACL-verified descriptor with post-read path/metadata and ACL rechecks (CodeQL #82). No Windows-native verification or CodeQL alert closure is claimed before public release.

Reject unexpected, duplicate, or incomplete assets in an existing GitHub Release before retrying publication or recovery; verify the exact five original release payload/provenance files again before dispatching the checksum signer.

Preserve npm trusted publishing, signed checksums, version/source parity, private review and Kubernetes rollout gates. This candidate is not proof of a higher OpenSSF score or an already deployed change; official rescanning and real public Action runs are required.

Keep existing device credentials, Windows DLL-free source-only interop, explicit screen-sharing consent and remote control/E2EE restrictions. No new capture permissions or native binaries are enabled.
